title: 3rd-Party App Governance: governing third-party apps, add-ons and extensions connected to SaaS platforms, and its portal, roles and dashboard

what-it-is.statement: 3rd-Party App Governance discovers, manages, reduces and controls the attack surface that third-party apps, extensions and add-ons introduce to corporate SaaS applications, and keeps an app inventory showing what is connected, the risks posed and how each app is used.

quotes: Zscaler 3rd-Party App Governance allows you to discover, manage, reduce, and control the attack surface introduced by third-party apps, extensions, and add-ons to corporate SaaS applications.
With 3rd-Party App Governance, you can uncover and maintain an up-to-date app inventory, gaining full visibility into what is connected, the risks posed, and how each app is used in your environment.

capabilities.statement: It classifies apps as sanctioned or unsanctioned, alerts on drift in app usage or security posture, notifies when apps are introduced in violation of corporate policy or compliance, and can run remediation such as banning an app or revoking its token manually or automatically, with end users involved in review. It gives visibility over first-, second- and third-party API integrations.

quotes: classifying apps as sanctioned or unsanctioned; monitoring and receiving alerts on drift in app usage or security posture; and receiving notifications when apps are introduced in violation of corporate policy or compliance.
You can manually or automatically streamline remediation actions such as banning or revoking an app token, and involve end users in the review process.
Gain full visibility over first-, second-, and third-party API integrations across your business so you can uncover dangerous SaaS platform connections.

portal-access.statement: The 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal is reached upon invitation, at https://apptotal.zscaler.com/. The configuration guide's prerequisite is authorization to access the portal, with the Zscaler Account team as the contact.

quotes: You can access 3rd-Party App Governance upon invitation.
Click Start Now in the 3rd-Party App Governance invitation email, or go to https://apptotal.zscaler.com/.
You must be authorized to access the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal. Contact your Zscaler Account team for more information.

sign-in-methods.statement: The Admin Portal page says authentication is performed using Google, Azure AD federation or Okta, that passwords are not supported, and that SAML federation with the customer's own identity provider is supported on enterprise tiers.

quotes: Authentication is performed using Google, Azure AD federation, or Okta. Passwords are not supported. SAML federation with your own identity provider (IdP) (e.g., Okta) is supported on enterprise tiers.

admin-console-sso.statement: From the Zscaler Admin Console the portal opens by SSO for subscribers to the 3rd-Party App Governance service, at Analytics > Reports > SaaS Security Report > 3rd-Party App Governance. It also requires access to the Data Loss Prevention (DLP) feature and a 3rd-Party App Governance Admin or a Super Admin role, and with a subscription it can be reached from several locations on the SaaS Security Report and SaaS Assets Report.

quotes: You can access the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal from the Zscaler Admin Console using SSO, if you have subscribed to the 3rd-Party App Governance service.
You must also have access to the Data Loss Prevention (DLP) feature and a 3rd-Party App Governance Admin or a Super Admin role assigned to you.
go to Analytics > Reports > SaaS Security Report > 3rd-Party App Governance.
You can also access the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal from multiple locations on the SaaS Security Report and SaaS Assets Report, if you have a subscription to 3rd-Party App Governance.

report-gate.statement: The 3rd-Party App Governance Report identifies all the third-party applications that employees are using, for the tenant selected under the Tenant option. With the Advanced Posture Management license enabled the user is redirected to the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal; without it, the report page is visible with an upgrade banner.

quotes: The 3rd-Party App Governance Report identifies all the third-party applications that employees are using.
The data is displayed for the tenant you select under the Tenant option.
If you have the Advanced Posture Management license enabled, you are redirected to the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal.
If you don't have the Advanced Posture Management license enabled, the 3rd-Party App Governance Report page with an upgrade banner is visible.

report-states.statement: The report's application states are Discovered (discovered, but no action taken yet), Allowed (explicitly allowed), Blocked (explicitly blocked), Restricted (an admin has allowed the application to specific users) and Reauthorized.

quotes: Discovered: The number of third-party applications discovered, but no action is taken on them yet.
Allowed: The number of applications explicitly allowed for use.
Blocked: The number of applications explicitly blocked for use.
Restricted: An admin has allowed the use of this application to specific users.
Reauthorized: The number of reauthorized applications for use. (e.g., the user had explicitly blocked the application earlier).

report-actions.statement: On the report's application page an admin can allow the use of the application for all users, restrict it to specific users, or revoke it for all users (the Blocked state), and can download a CSV file with all the permissions listed.

quotes: Allow Authorization for All Users: Allow the use of this application for all users.
Restrict Authorization to Specific Users: Restrict the use of this application to specific users.
Revoke Authorization for All Users: Revoke the use of this application for all users (this is the state Blocked).
Download: Download a CSV file with all the permissions listed.

portal-audit-log.statement: The portal has an Audit Log icon that shows changes made by users and admins, and a Reports menu with predefined reports and custom reports.

quotes: Click the Audit Log icon to view details on changes made by users and admins in 3rd-Party App Governance.
Click Reports to view predefined, out-of-the-box reports or custom reports that you have created.

roles.statement: The page lists three predefined roles that can be assigned to users. Admin is the default super admin role with full access including user management, policy editing, integrations and security actions. User can edit policies, upload apps, export data and acknowledge findings but cannot manage platform-wide settings or integrations. Viewer can view data and export reports but cannot take action or make changes. Role assignments are managed through Zscaler Support.

quotes: 3rd-Party App Governance provides the following set of predefined roles and permissions that can be assigned to users:
Admin: The default super admin role with the highest level of privilege that has full access across the platform, including user management, policy editing, integrations, and security actions.
User: The user can perform key operational actions like editing policies, uploading apps, exporting data, and acknowledging findings, but cannot manage platform-wide settings or integrations.
Viewer: The user can view data across the platform and export reports, but cannot take any action or make changes.
To manage role assignments, contact Zscaler Support.

license-dependent.statement: Connecting a platform, alerting through outbound integrations such as Slack, the automated workflow in policies (supported on Google and partially on Microsoft) and the contents of the App Panel each depend on the 3rd-Party App Governance license.

quotes: Connecting your platform to 3rd-Party App Governance is dependent on your license.
Alerting via outbound integrations such as Slack is dependent on your license.
Automated workflow is supported on Google and partially on Microsoft and is dependent on your license.
The contents of the App Panel vary depending on your 3rd-Party App Governance license.

widgets.statement: The dashboard contains 7 predefined widgets with information about potentially risky apps and their usage among users. When first accessed it is empty until a platform is connected or apps are searched for and added manually.

quotes: The dashboard contains 7 predefined widgets with information about potentially risky apps and their usage among your users.
When you first access the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal, the dashboard is empty until you connect your platform by clicking Connect, or search for and manually add apps.

integrations-banner.statement: The integrations banner has an All button clicked by default, so the dashboard shows the status of all integrations, and it appears on all pages of the portal. It can filter platforms by labels such as Legacy, Staging and Production, and shows a Pending icon while onboarded tenants are being processed and an Error icon on an error. Adding or managing labels needs user or admin permissions.

quotes: as well as an All button that is clicked by default, so the dashboard displays the status for all integrations. This banner appears on all pages across the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal.
Filter by Label: Click this button to filter the platforms by labels such as Legacy, Staging, and Production.

When a single tenant or multiple tenants are onboarded, a Pending icon appears next to the tenants and the relevant platform to indicate that the tenants are still being processed. An Error icon appears next to the tenants and the relevant platform to indicate an error.
You must have user or admin permissions to add or manage labels.

overview-widget.statement: The Overview widget shows the number of active apps, the number of apps classified as risky, the number of users affected by risky apps and the number of deactivated apps, with a filter for the number of active apps over a time period, and a breakdown of apps by whether they are potentially harmful, dormant or overprivileged.

quotes: Active Apps: Shows the number of active apps.
Risky Apps: Shows the number of apps that are classified as risky.
Affected Users: Shows the number of users who are affected by the risky apps.
Deactivated Apps: Shows the number of deactivated apps.
You can use the filter to view the number of active apps over a specific time period.
Apps by Finding Type: Shows a breakdown of apps by whether they are potentially harmful, dormant, or overprivileged.

highlights-widget.statement: The dashboard defines findings as security posture issues identified in an app that indicate their risk and severity, lists the latest app activities ordered by severity as Top Security Events, and says most insights concern breaches, credentials exposure or any event that puts the app's or publisher's users at risk.

quotes: Findings are security posture issues identified in an app that indicate their risk and severity.
Top Security Events: A list of the latest app activities ordered by severity.
Most insights concern breaches, credentials exposure, or any event that puts the app's or publisher’s users at risk.

map-and-lists.statement: Drop-down menus on the dashboard display apps by either Severity or Usage, apps by Risk Score, Popularity, High Privilege or Low Usage, and users by VIP, Privileged, Apps or Findings.

quotes: Use the drop-down menu to display apps by either Severity or Usage.
Use the drop-down menu to display the apps by Risk Score, Popularity, High Privilege, or Low Usage.
Use the drop-down menu to display the users by VIP, Privileged, Apps, or Findings.

sign-in-providers.summary: One Admin Portal page lists Google, Azure AD federation or Okta as the authentication methods, and also tells the reader to click Sign in with Google or Sign in with Azure AD.

quotes: Authentication is performed using Google, Azure AD federation, or Okta.

positions.says: Authentication is performed using Google, Azure AD federation, or Okta.

quotes: On the sign-in page, click Sign in with Google or Sign in with Azure AD.

positions.says: The sign-in page step names Sign in with Google or Sign in with Azure AD, with no Okta option.

sign-in-providers.impact: The page does not say whether Okta sign-in appears as its own button or only through enterprise-tier SAML federation, so which sign-in options a user sees is not settled.

report-license-gate.summary: The Admin Console route into the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal is gated on a 3rd-Party App Governance subscription by the portal page and on the Advanced Posture Management license by the report page.

quotes: You can access the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal from the Zscaler Admin Console using SSO, if you have subscribed to the 3rd-Party App Governance service.
go to Analytics > Reports > SaaS Security Report > 3rd-Party App Governance.

positions.says: The portal page gates the SSO route from Analytics > Reports > SaaS Security Report > 3rd-Party App Governance on having subscribed to the 3rd-Party App Governance service.

quotes: If you have the Advanced Posture Management license enabled, you are redirected to the 3rd-Party App Governance Admin Portal.
(Analytics > Reports > SaaS Security Report > 3rd-Party App Governance)

positions.says: The report page redirects to the portal from Analytics > Reports > SaaS Security Report > 3rd-Party App Governance when the Advanced Posture Management license is enabled.

report-license-gate.impact: Which license opens the portal from the Admin Console is not settled, which bears on the open license-relationship gap here and in zia.sspm; a licensing answer has to name both.

role-mapping.title: How the Admin Console role maps to the portal roles
role-mapping.detail: The Admin Console route needs a 3rd-Party App Governance Admin or a Super Admin role, while the portal has Admin, User and Viewer roles managed by Zscaler Support. No captured page says how the two map.

license-relationship.title: How the 3rd-Party App Governance license relates to Advanced SSPM
license-relationship.detail: The portal page needs a 3rd-Party App Governance subscription while the report page names the Advanced Posture Management license for the same redirect (see the report-license-gate divergence), the portal's NSS logs are linked to Advanced SSPM elsewhere in the graph, and the portal page does not define the enterprise tiers that allow SAML. The captured pages do not say how the licenses relate.

retention.title: Retention and time ranges for the audit log, activities and dashboard graphs
retention.detail: The pages do not state how long the portal's Audit Log or Activities data is kept, or which time ranges the dashboard filter offers.
